Heard on I.A. No.10188 of 2024, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of
bail to the appellant - Manju Rao and I.A. No.12641 of 2024, which is first application for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant - Dilip Vishwakarma.

Appellants-Manju Rao and Dilip Vishwkarma are aggrieved of the judgment dated 22.03.2023,
passed by learned XIVth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, POCSO Act, Bhopal District Bhopal (M.P.), in Special Case No. 198/2021, whereby appellant - Manju Rao has been convicted for offence punishable under Section 16 read with Section 17 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with the fine of Rs.2,000/- and appellant - Dilip Vishwakarma has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376 (D) of IPC and Section 5(N) read with Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulations.

It is submitted that appellants have falsely been implicated on account of old rivalry.
Age of the prosecutrix is doubtful in view of the evidence of the prosecutrix and her mother.

It is further submitted that prosecutrix did not produce her school entry certificate or register that is the Dakhil Kharij Register but the school teacher who has been examined categorically stated that the prosecutrix had taken admission in 4th Class.
The prosecutrix admitted that she does not remember the name of the school in which she has studied in the 1st class.

There is further admission of the mother that admission of the prosecutrix was made by her Nana-Nani and they had not given any Manju Rao vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129775867/

sentences.text: Thus, age of the prosecutrix is doubtful.
DNA of Dilip Vishwakarma has not matched.
Mother of the prosecutrix admitted that she got married at the age of 15-16.
Thus, when all these factors are corroborated then age of the prosecutrix becomes doubtful.
There is no medical examination in regard to prosecutrix being blinded by using a palm etc.
In fact, Doctor (PW-12) in her report did not say anything about any injury caused to the eyes for any examination of the eyes conducted by such Doctor.
There are good chances of success of these appeals.
The disposal of the appeals will take considerable time.
It is, therefore, prayed that the sentence imposed on the present appellants be suspended and they be enlarged on bail.
Shri G.S. Thakur, learned Government Advocate for the State has 3 CRA-5033-2024 opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence.
Taking into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting anything on merit, the applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for their appearance before the Trial Court on 23.12.2024 and on such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence imposed upon the present appellants shall remain suspended and they shall be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
Accordingly, I.A. No.10188 of 2024 and I.A. No.12641 of 2024 are disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.
